title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the definition of 'courbes standard' over a field k, which are the objects whose moduli, the strata at infinity of M_{g,ν}, the manuscript studies. On the previous page a standard curve is X = X̂ \ I. Here X̂ is a projective curve with 1-dimensional components whose only singularities are ordinary double points (nodes), forming the set A. I is a finite set of smooth k-points (the punctures, or 'points à l'infini'). Pulling back along the normalization Y = normalization of X̂ gives two things: a finite set Ĩ mapping isomorphically onto I, and Ã = preimage of A, a degree-2 cover of A. That cover gives a fixed-point-free involution σ_Ã of Ã.

This page states the resulting dictionary (1).
(a) Y is a smooth projective curve, possibly disconnected.
(b) Ã and I are disjoint finite subsets of Y(k), equivalently finite étale subschemes Ã_k, I_k.
(c) σ is a free involution of Ã, so |Ã| is even.

Conversely, from (a)(b)(c) one rebuilds X by pinching. X is the quotient of Y \ I_k obtained by identifying each point a of Ã with σ(a). Categorically, p : Y \ I_k → X is universal in (Sch) among morphisms with p∘i∘σ = p∘i, where i : Ã_k → Y \ I_k. So X is the coequalizer of i and iσ, equivalently the pushout of Y \ I ← Ã → Ã/σ.

Conclusion: the groupoid of standard curves over k (isomorphisms only) is equivalent to the groupoid of systems (a)(b)(c). NB: X̂ itself is recovered as Y/σ, the pinching of the complete curve Y.

This is the combinatorial-geometric description of a nodal pointed curve by its normalization plus gluing data. It underlies the stratification of the boundary of the moduli space by dual graphs (clutching). The next page tries to extend it to an arbitrary base S, defining a standard curve over S by such data. Grothendieck then marks the claimed full faithfulness 'faux tel quel!'.
errors: The phrase 'ou encore' identifies finite subsets of Y(k) with finite étale subschemes. This holds only for k algebraically closed (or with all points rational); over a general k the étale-subscheme version is strictly more general. Implicitly k is assumed algebraically closed.

'Quotient of Y by σ' is an abuse of language: σ is defined only on Ã, so one means the pinching, i.e. the quotient by the equivalence relation generated by a ~ σ(a). Its existence in (Sch) is standard (Serre's construction in Groupes algébriques et corps de classes; Ferrand's pinching), but it is not proved here.
No real gap for the statement over a field. The relative version on the next page is flagged by Grothendieck himself as false as stated.

ideas.what: Description of a nodal curve with punctures by its normalization, the preimage of the nodes with a free involution, and the puncture set; reconstruction by pinching, as an equivalence of groupoids.
ideas.modern_name: Normalization/clutching description of prestable pointed curves; dual-graph stratification of the boundary of M̄_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen (1983, clutching morphisms); pinching formalized by Ferrand (2003)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA explicitly; Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν} only informally

ideas.what: Characterization of X as a coequalizer in (Sch) of i and iσ (universal property of the pinching).
ideas.modern_name: Pushout / pinching of schemes along a finite subscheme
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Groupes algébriques et corps de classes, 1959); Ferrand 'Conducteur, descente et pincement' (2003)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard textbook description of nodal pointed curves via normalization and gluing data. Interesting only as preparatory set-up for the boundary-strata analysis; nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Ã_*' in the image should read 'Ã_k' (two finite étale disjoint subschemes Ã_k and I_k of Y).
The equation label to the left of the brace appears to be '(4)' (overwritten), not '(1)'. This is consistent with the next page using (5) and (6).
'Une courbe projective et lisse Y(=X̂̃)' is followed by a crossed-out word, correctly rendered as [-...-].
